text:
Alpha Centauri is a nearby stellar system, and Beta Pictoris is a young star with a debris disk. Observers record the pair when they discuss proper motion, radial velocity, and catalog cross-matches. The Greek letters α and β stay in the prose because they identify the stars in Bayer notation.

A report may say that the relative speed is -2.5 km/s and that the distance is about 1.3 pc. The solar mass is written M_⊙ and the solar luminosity is written L_⊙. Coordinates in this note are 14h 39m and −60° 50′, with the minus sign kept on the declination. NGC 1300 and M31 appear here only as examples of catalog style, not as claims about those galaxies.
title: Alpha Centauri fixture
